questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

I have written (1)/ a letter for the issue (2)/ of sports equipments. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option '3'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• The correct usage is 'sports equipment', not 'sports equipments'.
 
• The word 'equipment' is uncountable noun
 
• Thus, **equipments** will be replace with** equipment.**
 
• So, the corrected sentence should be: **"I have written a letter for the issue of sports equipment."**

questions.solution:

• The error lies in the use of the article **"the" **before **"sea."**

• Therefore, it should be **"in the sea" instead of "in sea."**

Thus, the correct answer is** "option 3".**

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

The decoration (1) / on the wall (2) / were a horse painting. (3) / no error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject of the sentence is** "The decoration"**, which is singular. **"on the wall"** is a prepositional phrase that tells about the subject.
 
• Therefore, the correct verb to use is "was", not "were" to match the singular subject.

**So, the corrected sentence is** "The decoration on the wall was a horse painting."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In this type of sentences we often confuse with the subject.
 
 
• **For example:** The books on the shelf in the library were all about science.
 
 
 
• Here "The books" is the subject, which is plural. The linking verb 'were' is correct usage.

**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

He leans (1)/ forward to (2)/ shut the door. (3) / no error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• Since the sentence makes complete grammatical and logical sense, there is no error.
 
• The sentence says "He leans forward to shut the door" means that a man is adjusting his position, moving himself forward, in order to close the door.
 
• 'He' is the third person singular number subject. 'leans' is the verb and grammatically correct. "Leans forward to" is the verb phrase describing the action he is performing.
 
• "Shut the door" is the objective of his action - the reason or purpose for his leaning forward.

Hence, the correct answer is** option 4.**

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

'Sunaina read the novel in four hours.'

options.text: The novel had been read by Sunaina in four hours.
The novel was read by Sunaina in four hours.
The novel has been reading by Sunaina within four hours.
The novel is read by Sunaina in four hours.

questions.solution:
The given sentence is in Active Voice, since the verb (read) indicates that its subject (Sunaina) did something to an object (novel).

Hence, changing it to Passive Voice, the verb should be changed to passive from active. The object of the transitive verb in the Active Voice should become the subject of the verb in the Passive Voice. 

Therefore, the same sentence in Passive Voice is:

The novel was read by Sunaina in four hours.

Hence, the correct answer is **option 2.**

questions.solution:

*The supporters of the ruling party thronged the streets.*

Hence, the correct answer is **option 1**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

The boats sail _________ the river.
questions.solution:
**‘**Sail in’ is used while talking about something that is contained or enclosed within something.

‘Sail on’ is used while talking about something that is resting on a surface.

Above is used for something that is at or to a higher place or position than something/somebody.

‘Sail to’ is used while talking about a particular destination that the boats are sailing towards.

Hence, the correct answer is **option 1**, that is **sail in**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

One should not question _________ does not concern him/her.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__what__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **What: **You use **what** after certain words, especially verbs and adjectives, when you are referring to a situation that is unknown or has not been specified.

 **Example: **I want to know what happened to Norman.
 
• **That: **You can use that after many verbs, adjectives, nouns, and expressions to introduce a clause in which you report what someone has said, or what they think or feel.

 **Example: **We were worried that she was going to die.
 
• **Which: **You use which to refer back to an idea or situation expressed in a previous sentence or sentences, especially when you want to give your opinion about it.
 
• **Whatever: **You use whatever to refer to anything or everything of a particular type.
 
• Since we are referring to a situation that is unknown or has not been specified, 'what' is the most appropriate option to use here.
